title: Suggestion deployment safeguards and revert playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a standardized safeguards + revert playbook for automatically-applied Optimize suggestions (batching, KV caching, quantization profiles). Goal: let the Optimize engine safely push low-risk configuration changes while ensuring predictable cost savings and minimal quality regressions. This ticket covers policy definitions, canary traffic schedule, acceptance gates (dry-run and live metrics), approval criteria, and a runbook for immediate rollback and postmortem capture.
goals: Define a gated rollout schedule for suggestion auto-applies (micro-canary -> progressive ramp) and circuit-breaker thresholds
Create a lightweight dry-run simulation and shadow routing path to validate performance/cost/quality before any live traffic shift
Formalize approval rules (auto-approve vs manual review) based on cost delta and quality delta from evaluation harness
Deliver a clear rollback playbook and automated rollback tooling hooks for console and runtime
Produce observability dashboards and alerting tied to each rollout stage
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can express suggestion rules with fields: cost_estimate_pct, quality_risk_score, allowed_traffic_stages
Dry-run simulation produces daily quality and cost delta report with pass/fail flag
Automated canary deployment controller supports traffic splits: 0.5%, 2%, 10%, 50%, 100% with configurable dwell times
Circuit-breaker triggers rollback when any of: p95 latency increases >30%, error_rate >0.25%, sample_quality_drop >1.0% or unexpected cost increase
Approval workflow enforced: suggestions with cost savings <10% or quality_risk_score >0.7 require PM/Eng approval
Rollback can be executed by a single API call and produces an audit entry with reason and snapshot of configs
tasks: Design policy schema for suggestion metadata (fields: variant_id, resource_profile, cost_estimate, quality_estimate, dry_run_artifact)
Extend Optimize backend to emit a dry-run simulation artifact and synthetic eval results
Implement canary controller in the rollout orchestrator and integrate with routing layer
Wire approval rules into Console UI and expose CLI endpoint for manual approvals/rejects
Add monitoring dashboards: cost delta, p95 latency, error rate, sample quality score and traffic stage visualization
Author rollback playbook and add automated rollback API that reverses to last pinned config and notifies stakeholders
rollout_plan: 1) Dry-run: run suggestion in shadow for 24h against production traffic with full KV cache and batching enabled; collect cost/quality deltas. 2) Canary stage: apply change to 0.5% traffic for 30m. If all metrics stable, move to 2% for 1h, then 10% for 2h, 50% for 6h, 100% after 24h. 3) Gates: each stage checks p95 latency, error rate, sample_quality_score, regression window for prompt sets. 4) Circuit-breaker: immediate rollback on failed gate. 5) Finalize: mark suggestion applied, create changelog entry and optional RFC for significant savings.
dry_run_requirements: Dry-run must execute real requests in shadow mode (no user-visible side effects)
Synthetics: evaluate against stored prompt suite and compute sample_quality_score and BLEU-like metrics
Cost projection: report estimated per-token cost delta and projected monthly savings for customer tier
approval_rules: Auto-approve when cost_estimate_pct >= 20% AND quality_risk_score <= 0.25 AND dry_run_pass == true
Require PM approval when cost_estimate_pct between 10% and 20% OR quality_risk_score between 0.25 and 0.6
Block auto-apply and escalate to SRE/Runtime if quality_risk_score > 0.6 or dry_run_pass == false
Allow emergency auto-rollback if circuit-breaker condition met during any canary stage
alerting: Page SRE on p95_latency_ms increase >30% sustained for 5m
Notify product and owner on sample_quality_score drop >1.0% in a stage
Create high-priority ticket if dry_run fails or simulation data missing
rollback_steps: 1) Halt the current rollout stage and freeze traffic shifts
2) Execute rollback API to revert to previous pinned configuration variant
3) Increase capacity on fallback pathway if necessary and verify routes
4) Open incident in PagerDuty with prefilled template and link to suggestion ID
5) Publish postmortem stub in the console with telemetry snapshots and any operator notes
6) Block re-apply of the same suggestion for 24 hours and flag for manual review
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic and approval rules
Integration test: shadow dry-run pipeline end-to-end with synthetic traffic
Canary simulation environment that runs staged traffic splits and validates circuit-breaker behavior
Chaos test: inject latency and errors during canary to validate automatic rollback
E2E QA with a synthetic customer org verifying Console approval flow and audit logs
risks: False-positive dry-run passes resulting in quality regressions on niche prompt distributions
Too-aggressive auto-approve thresholds could cause customer-facing regressions
Insufficient observability during short dwell times may miss flakiness
Operational complexity across Dedicated and Private deployments (networking/routing differences)
review_feedback: Lina Gomez (Lead SRE): add an explicit traffic shadow TTL and ensure dry-run doesn't rely on cached user state
Ravi Menon (PM): tighten auto-approve threshold for customer-facing models and require PM approval for savings affecting billing tier changes
Tess Nguyen (Research): add per-prompt bucketing in synthetic evals to detect distributional regressions
Sophie Laurent (Privacy): confirm dry-run artifacts are scrubbed of PII before storage
